First, a 38 is a whole lot more than an enhanced 22. 22 is 40 grains moving about 1100-1200fps. A 38 (standard) is usually 125 or 158 grains moving about 900fps. Huge difference in the energy. A +P is moving at (I think) 1100fps or so. It’s a significant enough step up. To be sure, a 22 can kill. But a 38 (especially a +P) can stop a person in their tracks. And I say ‘can’ because sometimes it might take a huge bullet to stop a person. But in most cases a +P will do the trick. I wouldn’t say a +P is halfway between a 38 and a 357, but maybe a good third of the way. It’s a cartridge developed for pistols originally chambered in 38 which could handle a little more but not a 357. But if you can, buy a pistol chambered for 357. Then you can shoot 38, 38+P, and 357 in it. Different billets for different applications.
